title: Manuel Perez's band at the Pekin and how it came to Chicago
summary: Howard lists the Perez band members, says Charlie Elgar brought them to Chicago, and dates joining at 1921, before his trumpet job.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And I played a G string melody and he'd play the variation, see. And then next course the whole band would come in there. That must have been beautiful. And what a trumpet player that Emmanuel Perez was. Strong horn, that's long. Yeah. Eddie Atkins, Louis Cantrell, Frank DeHeney. Eddie Atkins was a trombone player? Yeah. And what a trombone player. I love his work. Who else? Louis Cantrell, drums. He was an old man by then.

I forget the bass player. I don't know what a little. I didn't know Louis Cantrell played in Chicago. Heck yes. But that band. Charlie Elder was responsible for that band coming there. They played at a place in Chicago on Madison Street called El Sonia.
Yeah, I heard about that. And they come from El Sonia to the Pekin and I come from Dreamland.

And I came from Dreamland. And I came from the Pekin and I came from Dreamland. And I came from the Pekin and I came from the Pekin and I came from the Pekin. And I came from the Pekin and joined them at the Pekin.

You mean from the Dreamland ballroom? Yeah. And you would play with them later at night? At the Pekin, that's right. You would go home and change and go to the Pekin? No, I wouldn't change from there. No? Tuxedo? No.
That didn't change that. Table tuxedo?
That's right. Because they had on tuxedos.
What year was this to people? Oh geez.

21, I think it was 1921. 21. It was before I went to the Dreamland with this trumpet business. About six months before that. So how did you happen to play trumpet? Army. Oh the Army, that's right. You told me that.
